title: Fiona the hippo dies after ingesting knitted hat at Cincinnati zoo
summary:
Zoo staff tried a colonoscopy, vibration plate and other procedures to aid the hippo in passing the hat to no avail

Fiona the hippo, one of America’s most famous zoo animals, has died after…

blocks.text: Fiona the hippo, one of America’s most famous zoo animals, has died after efforts to remove a knitted hat that she swallowed after it fell into her enclosure proved unsuccessful.
With surgery too risky for a full-grown hippos like Fiona, who weighed in the region of 2,500lb (1,113kg), veterinarians tried alternative method of getting the hat to pass through her system.

The hat fell near Fiona when a visitor to the Cincinnati zoo tossed it in the air, after which it bounced it off a ceiling fan and fell into the enclosure, according to the Associated Press. Fiona ate the hat and was initially asymptomatic.
Days later, however, she began to lose appetite and staff at the zoo were forced to feed Fiona more in the hope that she would eventually get the hat through her digestive system.
The zoo announced on Wednesday that the animal care team was using a vibration plate from a horse farm to help move things along, according to the Associated Press.

Fiona was sedated a second time on Tuesday for evaluation. After an ultrasound, veterinarians could see her intestines still trying push the hat through. They also used a 9ft scope colonoscopy to view her intestines as well.

“The hope is that the vibrations will help encourage movement through her digestive tract and help the object pass,” the zoo said on social media. Fiona remained out of her enclosure while she was receiving treatment.
Footage from the procedure released by the zoo on Wednesday shows her snorting and moving around her enclosure, which vets said was a sign of progress. Her hydration levels were being monitored.

“Her care team even offered her a sniff of coffee, a scent she has always liked, and they were happy to see her respond. Thank you for your continued love and concern for Fiona and her dedicated care team,” the zoo said.

This wasn’t not the first time Fiona’s health has been at risk. She became a global sensation after her premature birth in 2017, when she couldn’t stand on her own and weighed just 29lb at birth, 25lb less than the lowest recorded birth weight for her species.

Fiona’s recovery had garnered support from across the country including, apparently, from Timothy, another hippo at the San Antonio zoo. Timothy sent well wishes via Instagram. “I know you’ve got some amazing people looking after you. We’re sending lots of love from Texas to the most beautiful hippo in the world. Hope you’re feeling more like yourself soon!”
Zoo staff had said updates on Fiona’s rally back to health would come as they received more information, reminding visitors to be careful when near habitats and to secure belongings.
In the meantime, the zoo asked visitors: “If something falls into a habitat, please notify a zoo staff member immediately.”
